destination.title: Calabi–Yau geometry, mirror constructions and moduli
destination.question: How can geometric, enumerative and field-theoretic constructions describe Calabi–Yau spaces, their moduli and their compactification applications?
destination.summary: A connected research neighborhood links explicit geometry, mirror calculations, quantum corrections, degeneration theory and compactification constraints. Its mathematical and integrable-model boundaries remain useful connections. No original region statement was supplied, so the original numerical membership is assessed separately from this newly proposed scope.

systems: Calabi–Yau threefolds and fourfolds, with dimensions retained separately
Local surface geometries, GLSMs and related Kähler sigma models
Specified heterotic, Type IIB, M-theory and F-theory settings
targets: Periods, mirror maps, moduli metrics and quantum couplings
Enumerative invariants, degeneration structure and compactification data
regimes: Finite-volume, infinite-volume and complex-structure degenerations, distinguished source by source
assumptions: Membership indicates a proposed research connection, not a common theorem or identical physical problem
Conjectures, proposed extensions and restricted example calculations retain their original status
conventions: Local quantum-ring mirror symmetry is distinguished from SCFT equivalence
Source-specific coordinates, normalization and genus restrictions are not identified across papers
includes: Fourfold and non-strict-holonomy extensions when explicitly supplied
Method and comparison connections to adjacent mathematical questions
excludes: A universal construction valid for every Calabi–Yau or GLSM
Automatic equivalence of questions sharing Kähler, Hodge or mirror terminology
Promotion of source-parent relations into family-wide physical assumptions

sources.title: Toric K3-Fibred Calabi-Yau Manifolds with del Pezzo Divisors for String Compactifications

evidence.text: Which explicit K3-fibred Calabi–Yau three-folds have additional rigid divisors suitable for combining LARGE Volume Scenario (LVS) moduli stabilisation with chiral D-brane constructions?

sources.title: The Hodge Numbers of Divisors of Calabi-Yau Threefold Hypersurfaces

evidence.text: How can structure-sheaf cohomology h^i(O_D) of square-free divisors in toric Calabi–Yau threefold hypersurfaces be computed efficiently, including at large h^{1,1}, to supply data relevant to Euclidean-brane zero modes and nonperturbative superpotentials?

sources.title: Comparing elliptic and toric hypersurface Calabi-Yau threefolds at large Hodge numbers

evidence.text: How closely do elliptic Calabi–Yau threefolds constructed through Weierstrass/Tate tunings reproduce toric hypersurface constructions at large Hodge numbers, and how do Tate tunings correspond to polytope tops?

sources.title: Heterotic String Models on Smooth Calabi-Yau Threefolds

evidence.text: How do interchangeable pieces of reflexive polytopes explain repeated structures in Calabi–Yau Hodge plots, and how do smooth discrete CICY quotients form connected webs?

sources.title: Modular forms as classification invariants of 4D $ \mathcal{N} $ = 2 Heterotic-IIA dual vacua

evidence.text: Which modular invariants refine the lattice-and-Φ classification of branches of 4D N=2 Heterotic–IIA dual vacua, determine geometric topology, and sometimes distinguish diffeomorphic Calabi–Yau threefolds with different Kähler cones?

sources.title: Towards refining the topological strings on compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds

evidence.text: How can refined Gopakumar–Vafa numbers on compact elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau threefolds be defined and calculated, and how do refined holomorphic anomalies relate to modular anomalies and geometric curve counting?

sources.title: Analytic periods via twisted symmetric squares

evidence.text: Can symmetric-square structures replace local series and parameter derivatives by analytic genus-one and K3 periods, enabling explicit mirror-map inversion and exact boundary distances relevant to the refined Swampland Distance Conjecture?

sources.title: Symmetries of Calabi-Yau prepotentials with isomorphic flops

evidence.text: How do isomorphic flop reflections constrain Gopakumar–Vafa invariants and the instanton Kähler-moduli prepotential, and when can the resulting invariant functions be expressed through Jacobi theta functions?

sources.title: CYTools: A Software Package for Analyzing Calabi-Yau Manifolds

evidence.text: How can the computational chain from reflexive polytopes to Calabi–Yau hypersurface data be made efficient even at the largest Hodge numbers in the Kreuzer–Skarke database?

sources.title: Moduli space reconstruction and Weak Gravity

evidence.text: Can genus-zero Gopakumar–Vafa (GV) invariants reconstruct Kähler moduli spaces, including non-toric phases and Weyl identifications, and provide explicit tests of the lattice WGC in a BPS charge region?

sources.title: Reflections in the mirror: Studying infinite Coxeter symmetries of GV-invariants

evidence.text: How do permutations and flops to diffeomorphic Calabi–Yau threefolds generate infinite symmetries of Gopakumar–Vafa invariants, and how can these relations constrain higher-genus computations through the BCOV holomorphic anomaly equations?

sources.title: Mirror symmetry for two parameter models. 1.

evidence.text: How does mirror symmetry determine the quantum Kähler geometry of two-parameter Calabi–Yau threefolds, particularly singular boundary loci, the large complex structure limit, mirror maps, and genus-zero and genus-one instanton contributions?

sources.title: Mirror symmetry, mirror map and applications to Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces

evidence.text: How can toric geometry construct previously unavailable mirrors and determine mirror maps, Yukawa couplings and instanton invariants for Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces with several moduli?

sources.title: Mirror symmetry, mirror map and applications to complete intersection Calabi-Yau spaces

evidence.text: How can periods and Picard–Fuchs equations yield mirror maps, instanton-corrected Yukawa couplings and prepotentials for multiparameter complete-intersection Calabi–Yau spaces, together with genus-one predictions?

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a Picard-one Calabi–Yau threefold avoid rational curves? The section tests that assumption through a one-modulus cubic geometry and a genus-one topological index, because the projective intersection-hypersurface argument is unavailable.

sources.title: Toric K3-Fibred Calabi-Yau Manifolds with del Pezzo Divisors for String Compactifications

evidence.text: Scan reflexive lattice polytopes for codimension-one reflexive sections; triangulate using extended PALP, calculate ambient Mori cones, and use SINGULAR for hypersurface intersection rings.

sources.title: The Hodge Numbers of Divisors of Calabi-Yau Threefold Hypersurfaces

evidence.text: Appendix C gives an alternative, restricted computation for face-limited divisors, using Koszul sequences, Serre duality and lattice-point counting of toric line-bundle sections.

sources.title: Comparing elliptic and toric hypersurface Calabi-Yau threefolds at large Hodge numbers

evidence.text: 6D anomaly cancellation determines generic matter in many cases and supplies Hodge shifts at fixed base: Δh1,1 = Δr ≥ 0 and Δh2,1 = ΔV − ΔHcharged ≤ 0. Exotic representations require additional geometric analysis.

sources.title: Heterotic String Models on Smooth Calabi-Yau Threefolds

evidence.text: The bundle scan assembles integer Chern-class matrices through partial-sum slope and index filters, Bianchi constraints, and subsequent cohomology calculations. Surviving slope equations are solved exactly in most cases and numerically in the remainder.

sources.title: Modular forms as classification invariants of 4D $ \mathcal{N} $ = 2 Heterotic-IIA dual vacua

evidence.text: For an enhanced branch, Ψγ=−24/rank(R) times the sum of (∂SθR+δ)Φenh,[γ,δ]. Here ∂S is the Ramanujan–Serre derivative. Gauge thresholds involve (ΦÊ2−Ψ)/η24, while gravitational thresholds involve ΦÊ2/η24.

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Reduce scalar quotient volume to group covolume where justified, then use nonzero adjoint trace to obstruct a lattice. Keep any symmetric-branch lattice construction separate.

sources.title: Enumerating Calabi-Yau Manifolds: Placing Bounds on the Number of Diffeomorphism Classes in the Kreuzer-Skarke List

evidence.text: How many diffeomorphism classes occur among Kreuzer–Skarke Calabi–Yau threefolds of Picard number at most six, after identifying intersection forms and second Chern classes under integral changes of basis?

sources.title: Exact Computation of the Special Geometry for Calabi–Yau Hypersurfaces of Fermat Type

evidence.text: Can the special Kähler potential be computed explicitly for all polynomial complex-structure deformations of Fermat Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces, including the real structure needed to pair their periods?

sources.title: On Classifying the Divisor Involutions in Calabi-Yau Threefolds

evidence.text: Which Calabi–Yau threefold hypersurfaces with h^{1,1}≤4 admit divisor exchanges or special coordinate reflections producing nonzero orientifold-odd (1,1) cohomology, and which offer useful volume forms for type IIB models with odd moduli?

sources.title: Deformed WZW models and Hodge theory. Part I

evidence.text: Can the horizontality conditions defining a one-complex-parameter variation of polarized Hodge structures be realised as classical equations of motion of an integrable λ-deformed G/G model, using the charge operator to identify the sigma-model fields?

sources.title: K3 Fibrations and heterotic type II string duality

evidence.text: Why do elliptic j-functions appear in candidate heterotic–type II dual pairs, and can modular mirror maps, prepotential derivatives and instanton symmetries provide further evidence for this conjectured duality?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Can quantum consistency determine the positivity cone and the gauge sectors required by negative self-intersection?

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can one arithmetic structural requirement unify the necessary conditions for quantum-consistent N = 2 special geometry?

sources.title: Asymptotic String Compactifications: Periods, flux potentials, and the swampland

evidence.text: How can asymptotic Hodge theory organize Calabi–Yau periods and physical couplings near degenerations, enabling calculations of weak-gravity bounds and flux-moduli stabilization beyond large complex structure?

sources.title: GLSM for Calabi-Yau Manifolds of Berglund-Hubsch Type

evidence.text: How can special Kähler geometry for polynomial deformations of Berglund–Hübsch-type Calabi–Yau manifolds be computed from Landau–Ginzburg data, and can a mirror GLSM sphere partition function reproduce the resulting exponentiated Kähler potential?

sources.title: Heterotic String Compactifications on Half-flat Manifolds. II.

evidence.text: How are Kähler and complex-structure deformations represented in the appendix's Calabi–Yau geometry? The setting supplies complex moduli, a holomorphic three-form, and an internal metric for the identities that follow.

sources.title: Recent developments in heterotic compactifications

evidence.text: Does mirror symmetry extend from target spaces to heterotic target-bundle pairs, exchanging sheaf cohomology and quantum-corrected computations?

sources.title: Compactifications of moduli spaces inspired by mirror symmetry

evidence.text: Can the mirror description of complex-structure moduli through complexified Kähler structures supply natural semi-toric partial compactifications, including a minimal analogue of Satake–Baily–Borel and boundary descriptions beyond normal crossings?

sources.title: Asymptotic Flux Compactifications and the Swampland

evidence.text: How can the full Hodge filtration on primitive middle cohomology be represented near a Calabi–Yau fourfold degeneration where several local complex-structure coordinates approach i∞?

sources.title: Comments on the Emergence of 4D Topological Amplitudes in M-Theory

evidence.text: For the Quintic, does minimal subtraction of the divergent Gopakumar–Vafa sum give equivalent results in mirror complex-structure and physical Kähler coordinates, and can this prescription recover the classical linear contribution to F1?

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which Calabi–Yau threefold compactifications can avoid world-sheet instanton corrections? The section permits finite free quotients of tori and elliptic-curve–K3 products, so its geometric domain extends beyond simply connected threefolds of strict SU(3) holonomy.

sources.title: Mirror symmetry

evidence.text: How can supersymmetric phase T-duality and vortex dynamics derive mirror descriptions of two-dimensional Kähler sigma models, including toric targets, Calabi–Yau examples, positive-first-Chern-class models and holomorphic-isometry deformations?

sources.title: Non-birational twisted derived equivalences in abelian GLSMs

evidence.text: How can abelian GLSMs realize non-birational Kähler phases, and can homological projective duality (HPD) explain their geometric, Landau–Ginzburg, and noncommutative descriptions?

sources.title: First order description of black holes in moduli space

evidence.text: Can the invariant matching construction extend to N=2 theories whose special Kähler moduli spaces lack a homogeneous-coset description? The paper limits its explicit treatment to models with tractable invariant data.

sources.title: Euler Characteristics of Crepant Resolutions of Weierstrass Models

evidence.text: How can one compute Euler characteristics of crepant resolutions of singular Weierstrass G-models over smooth bases of arbitrary dimension, and specialize these results to Calabi–Yau Euler characteristics and threefold Hodge numbers?

sources.title: Orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds: divisor exchanges and multi-reflections

evidence.text: How can divisor exchanges and multiple coordinate reflections efficiently generate Type IIB Calabi–Yau orientifolds, including their fixed loci, O-plane types, equivariant Hodge numbers and candidates passing a restricted tadpole test?

sources.title: Local mirror symmetry: Calculations and interpretations

evidence.text: How should local mirror invariants of surfaces inside Calabi–Yau threefolds be defined, calculated in A- and B-models, and interpreted enumeratively, including suitable singular surfaces?

sources.title: Emergent strings from infinite distance limits

evidence.text: How does a finite-volume Kähler degeneration select a shrinking curve or surface fiber?

sources.title: Classifying Calabi–Yau Threefolds Using Infinite Distance Limits

evidence.text: Can the complete pattern of infinite-volume degenerations furnish a practical invariant grouping Calabi–Yau threefolds, distinguishing some homotopy types and exposing elliptic, K3 and nested fibrations?

sources.title: Sphere Partition Function of Calabi–Yau GLSMs

evidence.text: Can the exact sphere partition function of Calabi-Yau GLSMs be expressed using a common structure in geometric, Landau-Ginzburg and hybrid phases, with identifiable state spaces, pairings, Gamma classes and Givental I/J-functions?

sources.title: Complete classification of reflexive polyhedra in four-dimensions

evidence.text: Classify all four-dimensional reflexive lattice polytopes, calculate the Hodge-number pairs of the associated Calabi–Yau threefold hypersurfaces, and determine connectedness through singular transitions.

sources.title: Theory of Kahler gravity

evidence.text: Can a target-space theory of Kähler deformations realize the background-independence connection of N=2 topological theories, and reproduce supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SQM) or semiclassical A-model amplitudes?

sources.title: Beyond the Kähler cone

evidence.text: How can analytic continuation link nonlinear σ-models on birational Calabi–Yau threefolds, enlarge complexified Kähler moduli to the movable cone, and motivate control of the birational automorphism action?

sources.title: Calabi-Yau fourfolds for M theory and F theory compactifications

evidence.text: Which explicit Calabi-Yau fourfold deformation families support M- and F-theory compactifications, and how do their topology, instanton divisors, elliptic degenerations, transitions and quantum cohomology encode effective-theory properties?

destination.title: Dark-energy dynamics, representations and conditional consistency
destination.question: Which mechanisms produce dark-energy behavior, how can their dynamics be inferred, and under what model-specific assumptions can they satisfy observational or conjectural restrictions?
destination.summary: The original numerical grouping is useful as a heterogeneous family, but no original prose scope was supplied for exact validation. Its sources include ordinary scalar dynamics, effective geometric descriptions, observational methods, conjecture tests and adjacent early-universe questions. Membership supplies navigation, not scientific equivalence.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Can canonical scalar descriptions of phenomenological dark-energy fluids satisfy a conjectured Planck-scale excursion bound while retaining observationally preferred parameters? The paper tests three Chaplygin variants and one interacting, power-law decaying vacuum model.

sources.title: DBI-essence

evidence.text: Do dark-energy scalar models with a Dirac–Born–Infeld kinetic term admit scaling attractors, what tension and potential shapes support them, and can their late-time behavior provide viable dark energy with sub-Planckian field values?

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a dark-energy density determined by the future cosmological event horizon be represented by a canonical scalar obeying the assumed field-range bound?

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Which dark-energy histories admit the positive-kinetic-energy scalar representation used by the excursion test? For positive scalar density, φ̇² = (1+w)ρφ requires w ≥ −1.

sources.title: Constraining the interacting dark energy models from weak gravity conjecture and recent observations

evidence.text: For phenomenological interactions between dark matter and dark energy, how restrictive is the scalar-excursion condition attributed to the weak gravity conjecture compared with the paper’s supernova, BAO and CMB constraints?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can a rolling dilaton and volume modulus in the nonsupersymmetric heterotic example provide viable dark energy while preserving compactification?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can a supercritical parent dimension produce shallower effective dark-energy slopes?

sources.title: Dark Energy in the Swampland II

evidence.text: Can a slowly rolling scalar with an exponential potential account for dark energy while satisfying both observational slope limits and a conjectural lower restriction on potential steepness?

sources.title: Do We Live in the Swampland?

evidence.text: How can the present positive dark-energy density coexist with a conjecture excluding constant positive vacuum energy? The paper uses an extremely light rolling scalar with an exponential potential at the meV scale.

sources.title: The multi-feature universe: Large parameter space cosmology and the swampland

evidence.text: How much can inferred limits on the conjectural potential-gradient constant c weaken when additional cosmological degrees of freedom and dark-sector interactions are admitted?

sources.title: The swampland conjecture and the Higgs expectation value

evidence.text: Can a light scalar coupled to both dark energy and the Higgs potential satisfy a quantum-gravity-motivated gradient condition while keeping vacuum energy small and matter masses sufficiently stable?

sources.title: Finite-time Singularities in Swampland-related Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: The setting is late-time dark energy modeled by a canonical scalar with positive exponential potential on a flat homogeneous and isotropic universe. Its swampland connection is a reported constant-slope attractor identification; the paper does not enforce an explicit quantum-gravity inequality.

sources.title: Dark Energy and the Refined de Sitter Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a dark-energy scalar satisfy the negative-curvature branch while remaining observationally close to a cosmological constant? The example varies a hilltop height and tachyonic curvature, with its initial displacement controlling the amount of rolling.

sources.title: Beta function quintessence cosmological parameters and fundamental constants – II. Exponential and logarithmic dark energy potentials

evidence.text: Which observables establish time-dependent dark energy, and which can identify the shape of its scalar potential?

sources.title: Swampland Conjectures and Late-Time Cosmology

evidence.text: Do cosmological distance and perturbation measurements permit canonical dark energy with an order-one potential slope or negative curvature, and do inferred field excursions challenge a Planck-scale distance limit?

sources.title: Horndeski gravity in the swampland

evidence.text: Can derivative interactions and non-minimal gravitational coupling permit a viable dark-energy history with an order-one potential slope? The paper addresses this in one selected Horndeski ansatz by comparing cosmological histories with reconstructed equation-of-state constraints.

sources.title: Dark energy beyond quintessence: Constraints from the swampland

evidence.text: Can a minimally coupled cubic derivative interaction alter transient dark-energy evolution while retaining an exponential potential with λ=1?

sources.title: Dark energy beyond quintessence: Constraints from the swampland

evidence.text: Can a scalar with an order-one potential slope produce an observationally acceptable dark-energy history when cubic derivative interactions provide additional transient damping?

sources.title: Swampland criteria in the slotheon field dark energy

evidence.text: Can gravitational derivative coupling keep a scalar sufficiently slowly evolving to behave as dark energy even when its potential has an order-one normalized slope?

sources.title: Swampland criteria in the slotheon field dark energy

evidence.text: Does coupling a dark-energy scalar's derivatives to the Einstein tensor allow a steeper positive potential while retaining an equation of state compatible with observationally motivated bounds?

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: Can a scalar potential provide slowly evolving dark energy with density near 10^−120 MPl^4? The problem combines a tiny potential amplitude with sufficiently slow dynamics; satisfying one requirement does not establish the other.

sources.title: Pole Dark Energy

evidence.text: Can the small excursions and unusual canonical potential shapes of pole dark energy satisfy both a conjectured distance bound and an order-unity normalized gradient while producing w close to -1?

sources.title: Pole Dark Energy

evidence.text: Can a field-dependent kinetic pole make familiar scalar potentials produce dark energy sufficiently close to a cosmological constant, while retaining small field excursions and potentially satisfying conjectured quantum-gravity restrictions?

sources.title: Swampland and screened modified gravity

evidence.text: Can screened scalar-tensor dark-energy models satisfy the de Sitter and distance conjectures together with local gravity constraints, and what follows for their future cosmology?

sources.title: Warm dark energy

evidence.text: The setting tests whether energy transfer from a homogeneous rolling pseudoscalar to a U(1) gauge field supplies sufficient friction for dark-energy acceleration. The numerical example has an exponential potential and begins during matter domination.

sources.title: The distribution of vacua in random landscape potentials

evidence.text: Can soft directions near a low-energy minimum support slowly evolving dark energy? The paper proposes small curvatures and a hierarchy among a few fields as a possible mechanism, leaving cosmological evolution for future work.

sources.title: Scalar field emulator via anisotropically deformed vacuum energy: Application to dark energy

evidence.text: Can an anisotropic generalization of vacuum energy cooperate with expansion shear to emulate a canonical scalar field with arbitrary potential, while producing observable differences from scalar-field dark energy?

sources.title: Constraints on dark energy models from the Horndeski theory

evidence.text: Can a Horndeski dark-energy model containing scalar derivative self-interactions and derivative coupling to gravity produce viable late-time evolution while satisfying the historical dark-energy and gravitational-wave speed constraints used by the authors?

sources.title: Out of the Swampland with Multifield Quintessence?

evidence.text: Can curved two-field dynamics reconcile accelerated expansion with a steep potential and a conjectured quantum-gravity gradient bound? The application is late-time dark energy; a complete ultraviolet realization remains a separate unresolved requirement.

sources.title: Out of the Swampland with Multifield Quintessence?

evidence.text: The setting tests how a curved scalar kinetic metric changes dark-energy evolution. Only φ1 experiences a potential, but motion in the exactly flat φ2 direction acts back on φ1 through its kinetic coupling.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Absorb the phenomenological interaction into an effective vacuum pressure, reconstruct a canonical background scalar from that effective stress tensor, and integrate its redshift derivative. Changing the decay law requires solving the interaction and background again.

sources.title: DBI-essence

evidence.text: Impose constant scalar equation of state and ρφ∝a^{-3(1+ωφ)} in a fluid-dominated background. Integrate the resulting field evolution, then use the DBI field equation to determine the tension and potential for the constant-γ branch.

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Translate the component's density and equation of state into its canonical field speed, change the integration variable to redshift, and integrate. Apply the field-range conjecture to that excursion rather than directly to w.

sources.title: Constraining the interacting dark energy models from weak gravity conjecture and recent observations

evidence.text: The theoretical selection is Δφ(zm)/Mp=∫₀^zm sqrt(3|(1+w(z))Ωφ(z)|) dz/(1+z)<1. The paper integrates the model evolution and evaluates this condition, normally taking zm=1090.

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Fit observations directly in the physical model's parameter space with Bayesian MCMC, and independently profile the likelihood for the reported single-exponential check. This retains model information omitted by the envelope comparison.

sources.title: Dark Energy in the Swampland II

evidence.text: Transform the ellipsoid to a Euclidean ball, apply Cauchy-Schwarz, and inspect rotations at fixed eigenvalues. This agent abstraction isolates the geometrical mechanism behind possible sensitivity without claiming the paper used this exact formula.

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture for the Effective Field Theories with N Species

evidence.text: Does the equal-field assisted trajectory admit slow evolution when the collective energy density must remain below the conjectured scalar cutoff?

sources.title: Building Supergravity Quintessence Model

evidence.text: The conjecture motivates replacing a positive cosmological constant with an evolving scalar and provides a proposed quantum-gravity test for a very flat dark-energy potential.

sources.title: Multi-field dark energy: Cosmic acceleration on a steep potential

evidence.text: Several scalar degrees of freedom supply dark energy while their kinetic terms define a field-space geometry. Matter and radiation remain present, so slowly evolving scalar energy need not imply that the total universe is already accelerating.

sources.title: Swampland conjectures and slow-roll thawing quintessence

evidence.text: Determine whether a canonical scalar that begins nearly frozen can explain dark energy while meeting the paper's distance and refined de Sitter conditions. Assess how compatibility depends on initial slope, potential curvature, and observational priors.

sources.title: Multifield Cosmology and the Dark Universe

evidence.text: What cosmological effects arise from strongly non-geodesic multifield trajectories, and can reviewed exact inspiraling dark-energy solutions produce observable perturbation effects and potentially alleviate the Hubble and σ8 tensions?

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture and Holographic/Agegraphic Dark Energy

evidence.text: Can WGC-motivated bounds on canonical scalar excursions be reformulated using the defining infrared cutoffs of holographic dark energy (HDE) and new agegraphic dark energy (NADE), thereby alleviating their reported tension with the bound |Δφ|≤Mp?

sources.title: Cosmological dynamics of multifield dark energy

evidence.text: How does field-space geometry change the homogeneous evolution of minimally coupled scalar dark energy in an expanding universe?

sources.title: Swampland Conjectures and Late-Time Cosmology

evidence.text: How much can a canonical dark-energy scalar evolve while preserving the observed late-time expansion and linear perturbations?

sources.title: Quintessence dynamics with two scalar fields and mixed kinetic terms

evidence.text: How does a mixed kinetic term change the critical points, stability and dark-energy evolution of two scalar fields with additive or multiplicative exponential potentials, including whether the scalar equation of state can approach −1?

sources.title: Warm dark energy

evidence.text: Can production of an additional field slow a dark-energy scalar enough to accelerate the Universe when its potential is too steep for Hubble friction alone? Conventional quintessence and tracking models motivate the question but retain a very small scalar curvature scale.

sources.title: Dark Energy, the Swampland and the Equivalence Principle

evidence.text: Can early suppression of a scalar-mediated dark-matter force permit appreciable attraction today while retaining acceptable expansion and structure formation? The paper also asks whether the interaction can slow quintessence sufficiently to accommodate a larger exponential-potential slope.

sources.title: New accelerating solutions in late-time cosmology

evidence.text: Can curved two-field dynamics generate stable late-time acceleration and observationally acceptable dark-energy transients even when the scalar potential is steep?

sources.title: The multi-feature universe: Large parameter space cosmology and the swampland

evidence.text: Does admitting curvature, neutrino physics, primordial-spectrum freedom, lensing rescaling, helium abundance and a phenomenological dark interaction change cosmological restrictions on dark-energy slopes and inflation?

sources.title: On finite time singularities in scalar field dark energy models based in the RS-II Braneworld

evidence.text: The setting asks how brane corrections to cosmological expansion affect singularities of scalar dark energy. A field-dependent kinetic coupling is introduced to cover more than a canonical scalar, while pressureless matter remains part of the cosmological energy budget.

sources.title: Assessing Cosmological Evidence for Nonminimal Coupling

evidence.text: Conditional on scalar-field dark energy, do the specified cosmological datasets favor negative potential curvature and nonminimal gravitational coupling, and can the resulting cosmology be reconciled with small-scale gravity constraints?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can transient motion between steep directions rescue a two-field potential whose shallowest asymptotic slope is too large? The displayed test includes matter, radiation, and initially stationary fields.

sources.title: Multi-field dark energy: Cosmic acceleration on a steep potential

evidence.text: Can dark energy remain dynamically active on a steep potential while its equation of state resembles a cosmological constant? The paper investigates whether turning in field space permits this behavior and whether fluctuations can distinguish it observationally.

sources.title: Hubble sinks in the low-redshift swampland

evidence.text: Can dark-matter coupling produce apparent phantom dark energy while the scalar remains canonical? The adopted present normalization fixes a nonphantom effective value today, while evolution at positive redshift can change that behavior.

sources.title: The Effective Potential Originating from Swampland and the Non-trivial Brans-Dicke Coupling

evidence.text: Does a cosmic-contortion dark-energy history admit an auxiliary scalar description, and how do the bare cosmological constant and curvature coupling affect the reconstructed potential?

sources.title: The Effects of Pole Dark Energy on Gravitational Waves

evidence.text: How does phenomenological pole dark energy affect the redshift evolution of the gravitational-wave variable η in a flat FRW universe, and what background solutions arise for power-law and exponential scalar potentials?

sources.title: Constraints on late time violations of the equivalence principle in the dark sector

evidence.text: How strongly do cosmological background and linear-perturbation observations constrain a dark-matter fifth force that activates near dark-energy domination, and does this interacting model improve compatibility with an order-one exponential-potential slope?

sources.title: Swampland criteria in the slotheon field dark energy

evidence.text: Which scalar potentials and field excursions are conjecturally compatible with quantum gravity, and how restrictive are those conditions for dark energy?

sources.title: Swampland criteria for a dark energy dominated universe ensuing from Gaussian processes and H(z) data analysis

evidence.text: Can Gaussian-process reconstruction of H(z) constrain the Swampland gradient constant c during dark-energy domination without choosing a scalar potential, and how do the inferred bounds depend on the kernel and H0?

sources.title: On the Cosmological Implications of the String Swampland

evidence.text: Determine whether early inflation, present dark energy and future expansion can obey simultaneous restrictions on scalar-field travel and positive-potential slope. The numerical strength of both restrictions remains an input rather than an established property of quantum gravity.

sources.title: Swampland conjectures and slow-roll thawing quintessence

evidence.text: A homogeneous canonical scalar can produce dynamical dark energy. Its motion follows the scalar equation with Hubble friction, while its departure from w = −1 measures kinetic energy relative to total scalar density.

sources.title: A stringy perspective on the coincidence problem

evidence.text: How rapidly does a canonical dark-energy field move after domination, and when can that motion expose additional light degrees of freedom?

sources.title: On the occurrence of finite-time singularities in swampland-related quintessence dark energy models

evidence.text: The setting asks how an interacting scalar dark-energy component behaves when dark matter and radiation are included in homogeneous flat cosmology. The exponential potential makes its logarithmic slope constant, enabling an autonomous representation.

sources.title: Reconstructing Quintessence

evidence.text: Determine which properties of a canonical dark-energy scalar can be inferred from cosmological observations without committing to a potential formula. The targets include its equation of state, traversed potential, field excursion and dynamical trajectories.

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: A rolling scalar can provide present acceleration without a positive stationary vacuum. The observationally allowed exponential supplies a small but nonzero field-space gradient whose scale is set by dark energy.

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: How strongly do observations constrain a nonphantom exponential dark-energy potential? The comparison concerns V0 e^{λφ}, rather than an unrestricted phenomenological equation of state.

sources.title: Reconstructing Quintessence

evidence.text: Test whether a reconstructed positive dark-energy potential is compatible with conjectural restrictions on its slope, curvature and field excursion.

sources.title: Pole Dark Energy

evidence.text: The model isolates the effect of a field-dependent kinetic normalization on scalar dark energy. Both the kinetic coefficient and the potential may be singular at the selected coordinate boundary.

sources.title: Emergent Dark Universe and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can the homogeneous stress tensor of a geometric dark fluid be reproduced by a canonical scalar potential, allowing scalar-potential diagnostics to be evaluated even though the original model contains no explicit scalar?

sources.title: Deciphering coupled scalar dark sectors

evidence.text: Can kinetic interactions from scalar field-space geometry be distinguished cosmologically from potential interactions, and can their cancellation conceal an interacting dark sector?

sources.title: Dark Energy in the Swampland II

evidence.text: How small can the exponential slope become before dark-energy observations lose the ability to distinguish the model from a cosmological constant?

destinations.title: Can canonical scalar descriptions of phenomenological dark-energy fluids satisfy a conjectured Planck-scale excursion bound while retaining observationally preferred parameters? The paper tests three Chaplygin variants and one interacting, power-law decaying vacuum model.

Do dark-energy scalar models with a Dirac–Born–Infeld kinetic term admit scaling attractors, what tension and potential shapes support them, and can their late-time behavior provide viable dark energy with sub-Planckian field values?
Can a dark-energy density determined by the future cosmological event horizon be represented by a canonical scalar obeying the assumed field-range bound?
Which dark-energy histories admit the positive-kinetic-energy scalar representation used by the excursion test? For positive scalar density, φ̇² = (1+w)ρφ requires w ≥ −1.

For phenomenological interactions between dark matter and dark energy, how restrictive is the scalar-excursion condition attributed to the weak gravity conjecture compared with the paper’s supernova, BAO and CMB constraints?
Can a rolling dilaton and volume modulus in the nonsupersymmetric heterotic example provide viable dark energy while preserving compactification?
Can a supercritical parent dimension produce shallower effective dark-energy slopes?
Can a slowly rolling scalar with an exponential potential account for dark energy while satisfying both observational slope limits and a conjectural lower restriction on potential steepness?

How can the present positive dark-energy density coexist with a conjecture excluding constant positive vacuum energy? The paper uses an extremely light rolling scalar with an exponential potential at the meV scale.
How much can inferred limits on the conjectural potential-gradient constant c weaken when additional cosmological degrees of freedom and dark-sector interactions are admitted?
Can a light scalar coupled to both dark energy and the Higgs potential satisfy a quantum-gravity-motivated gradient condition while keeping vacuum energy small and matter masses sufficiently stable?

The setting is late-time dark energy modeled by a canonical scalar with positive exponential potential on a flat homogeneous and isotropic universe. Its swampland connection is a reported constant-slope attractor identification; the paper does not enforce an explicit quantum-gravity inequality.

Can a dark-energy scalar satisfy the negative-curvature branch while remaining observationally close to a cosmological constant? The example varies a hilltop height and tachyonic curvature, with its initial displacement controlling the amount of rolling.
Which observables establish time-dependent dark energy, and which can identify the shape of its scalar potential?

Do cosmological distance and perturbation measurements permit canonical dark energy with an order-one potential slope or negative curvature, and do inferred field excursions challenge a Planck-scale distance limit?

Can derivative interactions and non-minimal gravitational coupling permit a viable dark-energy history with an order-one potential slope? The paper addresses this in one selected Horndeski ansatz by comparing cosmological histories with reconstructed equation-of-state constraints.
Can a minimally coupled cubic derivative interaction alter transient dark-energy evolution while retaining an exponential potential with λ=1?
Can a scalar with an order-one potential slope produce an observationally acceptable dark-energy history when cubic derivative interactions provide additional transient damping?
Can gravitational derivative coupling keep a scalar sufficiently slowly evolving to behave as dark energy even when its potential has an order-one normalized slope?
Does coupling a dark-energy scalar's derivatives to the Einstein tensor allow a steeper positive potential while retaining an equation of state compatible with observationally motivated bounds?

Can a scalar potential provide slowly evolving dark energy with density near 10^−120 MPl^4? The problem combines a tiny potential amplitude with sufficiently slow dynamics; satisfying one requirement does not establish the other.
Can the small excursions and unusual canonical potential shapes of pole dark energy satisfy both a conjectured distance bound and an order-unity normalized gradient while producing w close to -1?

Can a field-dependent kinetic pole make familiar scalar potentials produce dark energy sufficiently close to a cosmological constant, while retaining small field excursions and potentially satisfying conjectured quantum-gravity restrictions?
Can screened scalar-tensor dark-energy models satisfy the de Sitter and distance conjectures together with local gravity constraints, and what follows for their future cosmology?

The setting tests whether energy transfer from a homogeneous rolling pseudoscalar to a U(1) gauge field supplies sufficient friction for dark-energy acceleration. The numerical example has an exponential potential and begins during matter domination.

Can soft directions near a low-energy minimum support slowly evolving dark energy? The paper proposes small curvatures and a hierarchy among a few fields as a possible mechanism, leaving cosmological evolution for future work.

Can an anisotropic generalization of vacuum energy cooperate with expansion shear to emulate a canonical scalar field with arbitrary potential, while producing observable differences from scalar-field dark energy?

Can a Horndeski dark-energy model containing scalar derivative self-interactions and derivative coupling to gravity produce viable late-time evolution while satisfying the historical dark-energy and gravitational-wave speed constraints used by the authors?

Can curved two-field dynamics reconcile accelerated expansion with a steep potential and a conjectured quantum-gravity gradient bound? The application is late-time dark energy; a complete ultraviolet realization remains a separate unresolved requirement.

The setting tests how a curved scalar kinetic metric changes dark-energy evolution. Only φ1 experiences a potential, but motion in the exactly flat φ2 direction acts back on φ1 through its kinetic coupling.

A homogeneous canonical scalar can produce dynamical dark energy. Its motion follows the scalar equation with Hubble friction, while its departure from w = −1 measures kinetic energy relative to total scalar density.

Determine whether a canonical scalar that begins nearly frozen can explain dark energy while meeting the paper's distance and refined de Sitter conditions. Assess how compatibility depends on initial slope, potential curvature, and observational priors.

Several scalar degrees of freedom supply dark energy while their kinetic terms define a field-space geometry. Matter and radiation remain present, so slowly evolving scalar energy need not imply that the total universe is already accelerating.
Test whether a reconstructed positive dark-energy potential is compatible with conjectural restrictions on its slope, curvature and field excursion.

The setting asks how brane corrections to cosmological expansion affect singularities of scalar dark energy. A field-dependent kinetic coupling is introduced to cover more than a canonical scalar, while pressureless matter remains part of the cosmological energy budget.

How does phenomenological pole dark energy affect the redshift evolution of the gravitational-wave variable η in a flat FRW universe, and what background solutions arise for power-law and exponential scalar potentials?
Can kinetic interactions from scalar field-space geometry be distinguished cosmologically from potential interactions, and can their cancellation conceal an interacting dark sector?

Conditional on scalar-field dark energy, do the specified cosmological datasets favor negative potential curvature and nonminimal gravitational coupling, and can the resulting cosmology be reconciled with small-scale gravity constraints?
